hook.sub: The IRS looks at how you run it.

lines: So he skipped the tax part.

items.l: Hobby income goes on your return too

beats.kicker: Signs the IRS sees a business

items.t: You run it like a real business
items.s: Its own bank account, invoices and records.

items.t: You put in real time and effort
You change things to make a profit

beats.sub: Self-employment tax starts once net earnings reach $400.

captions.instagram:
Selling a few paintings a year still counts on your tax return.

✔️ Hobby income still goes on your federal return (Schedule 1, line 8j).
✔️ The IRS weighs several signs of a business: you run it like a real business, with real records, you put in real time and effort, you change your methods to make a profit, and you rely on the income.
✔️ A business reports on Schedule C: income minus ordinary business expenses like materials, booth fees and software.
✔️ Self-employment tax applies once net earnings reach $400 for the year.

captions.pinterest_alt: Short video: an artist sold 14 paintings and calls it a hobby; myth vs fact on hobby income, three signs the IRS sees a business, and Schedule C.

sources.fact: Hobby income must still be reported on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8j; signs of a business: businesslike manner and accurate records, substantial time and effort, intent to make a profit, relying on the income, prior profits (Taxpayer Advocate Service tax tip, March 2026, read 2026-10-24)
IRS factors: time and effort, profit history, businesslike books and records, changed methods to improve profitability, reliance on income (IRS Tax Tip 2024-55, read 2026-10-24)
Schedule SE and SE tax apply when net earnings from self-employment are $400 or more; rate 15.3% (read 2026-10-24)
